# shadcn-react-table

> A shadcn/ui data table with Material React Table parity — sorting, filtering, grouping, editing, virtualization, pinning, keyboard navigation and more — built on TanStack Table v9. It is a shadcn registry block: the source is copied into your project and uses your own shadcn components and theme.

Install into a project set up with shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS v4:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/r/data-table.json
```

Then `import { DataTable, useDataTable } from "@/components/ui/data-table"`: build the table with `const table = useDataTable({ data, columns, getRowId })` and render `<DataTable table={table} />`.

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/ -->

# Shadcn React Table

A **shadcn/ui data table** with [Material React Table](https://www.material-react-table.com/) (MRT V3) feature parity, built on [TanStack Table v9](https://tanstack.com/table/latest). It ships as a shadcn **registry** component — you install the source into your own project with the shadcn CLI, so it inherits your style, base color, and theme tokens and you own every line.

Example (`advanced`):

```tsx
function AdvancedExample() {
  const [data, setData] = React.useState(() => baseUsers)
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableRowSelection: true,
    enableMultiSort: true,
    enableColumnOrdering: true,
    enableColumnPinning: true,
    enableColumnResizing: true,
    enableRowNumbers: true,
    enableRowPinning: true,
    enableGrouping: true,
    enableStickyFooter: true,
    enableEditing: true,
    editDisplayMode: "row",
    initialState: { showColumnFilters: true, pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
    onEditingRowSave: ({ row, values, exit }) => {
      setData((prev) =>
        prev.map((r) =>
          r.id === row.id ? { ...r, ...(values as Partial<User>) } : r
        )
      )
      exit()
    },
    renderRowActions: ({ row }) => (
      <Button
        variant="ghost"
        size="icon-xs"
        aria-label="Delete row"
        onClick={() =>
          setData((prev) => prev.filter((r) => r.id !== row.original.id))
        }
      >
        <RiDeleteBinLine />
      </Button>
    ),
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

## Why this table

MRT is the most complete React table, but it's tied to Material UI. This table brings that same breadth of features to the shadcn/ui ecosystem:

- **One hook, one component.** `useDataTable(options)` returns an enriched TanStack instance; `<DataTable table={table} />` renders it. Everything is driven by options.
- **Feature-complete.** Sorting, per-column filtering with mode menus, fuzzy global search, column ordering / pinning / resizing / visibility, density, sticky header & footer, row selection, row numbers, row pinning, drag-to-reorder rows, grouping with aggregation, detail panels, tree data, inline editing (cell / row / table / modal), row & cell actions, click-to-copy, row & column virtualization, CSV / Excel export, full localization, and swappable icons.
- **Style-agnostic.** It only uses standard shadcn primitive APIs (`button`, `table`, `popover`, `command`, …), declared as registry dependencies. `shadcn add` installs them in _your_ configured style, so the table adopts your look with nothing to override.
- **You own the source.** No opaque dependency — the component lands in your repo under `components/ui/data-table/` and is yours to extend.

## How it works

It is a thin, opinionated layer over TanStack Table:

- It wraps TanStack's `useTable` with sensible defaults (row models wired for you, an auto-injected selection column, localization) and adds to the instance: its UI state in `table.getState()`, methods such as `table.setDensity`, and its resolved options on `table.dataTable`.
- Controlled state (`sorting`, `columnFilters`, `pagination`, `rowSelection`, …), the `manual*` server-side flags, and `getRowId` all **pass straight through** to TanStack. If you know TanStack Table, you already know this table.
- The `<DataTable />` component reads `table.dataTable` to render the toolbar, filter row, body, footer, and pagination — no prop drilling.

## For AI tools

Coding agents can install and use the table from one prompt, a skill file, the shadcn MCP server, or the docs as Markdown (`/llms.txt`, and `.md` after any page URL). See [AI agent setup](/docs/ai).

## Next steps

- [Installation](/docs/installation) — add the table to your project via the shadcn registry.
- [Quick start](/docs/quick-start) — a minimal table in a few lines.
- [Usage](/docs/usage) — the mental model: options in, instance out.
- [Guides](/docs/guides/sorting) — one page per feature, each with a live example.
- [API reference](/docs/api/use-data-table) — every option, prop, and token, generated from the source types.

# Installation

The data table is distributed as a **shadcn registry** item. The CLI installs the table source into your project, pulls the shadcn primitives it depends on (in *your* configured style), and installs the npm packages it needs.

## Prerequisites

- A project already set up with **shadcn/ui** (a `components.json` with your style, base color, and `@/components/ui` aliases). If you don't have one, run `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest init` first.
- **Tailwind CSS v4** and React 19 / Next.js (or any bundler that compiles your `components/`).

> **Any shadcn style works — Radix UI or Base UI:** It only uses standard primitive APIs, so it adapts to any shadcn style (Sera, Vega, Nova, Luma, …), base color, **and component library flavor**. The same URL works in Radix-flavored and Base-UI-flavored projects: a current shadcn CLI (4.x — the one with `init -b radix|base`) adapts the source to your flavor at install time and pulls the primitives in *your* style. Nothing is overwritten unless you opt in.

## Add the component

Run the shadcn CLI against the registry URL:

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/r/data-table.json
```

This single command:

1. **Installs npm dependencies** — `@tanstack/react-table@^9`, `@tanstack/react-virtual`, `@tanstack/match-sorter-utils@^9`, `@dnd-kit/*`, `date-fns`, `lucide-react`. The headless component library (Radix UI or Base UI) comes with the primitives below, matching your flavor.
2. **Pulls the shadcn primitives** it uses (`badge`, `button`, `calendar`, `checkbox`, `command`, `context-menu`, `dialog`, `dropdown-menu`, `input`, `label`, `popover`, `select`, `skeleton`, `slider`, `table`, `tooltip`) in your style — and skips any you already have.
3. **Writes the table** to `components/ui/data-table/`.
4. **Injects design tokens** (`--highlight`, `--highlight-foreground`) into your `globals.css`.

## Use a namespace (optional)

To install by name instead of URL, add the registry to your `components.json`:

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@shadcn-react-table": "https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

Then:

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @shadcn-react-table/data-table
# a language, e.g. German
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @shadcn-react-table/data-table-locale-de
```

## Verify

Import the public API from your `@/components/ui/data-table` alias:

```tsx
import { DataTable, useDataTable } from "@/components/ui/data-table"
```

> **react-day-picker v9+:** If your shadcn `calendar.tsx` predates react-day-picker v9, its `classNames` may use the old `table` key (renamed to `month_grid`). Re-run `shadcn add calendar` or rename the key — this only affects the date filter variant. The calendar itself comes from your own shadcn setup via `registryDependencies` — the table isn't tied to react-day-picker, and any calendar with a compatible props surface drops in.

## Next

Head to the [Quick start](/docs/quick-start) to render your first table.

# AI agent setup

Set up the data table with a coding agent — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot and the like.

## Ask your agent

Paste this into your agent:

```text
Install shadcn-react-table in my app: https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/SKILL.md
```

The prompt points the agent at the skill file: how to install the table (running `shadcn init` first when the project has no `components.json`), the rules that keep tables correct, where the option references are, and how to pull a docs example into the project. Every example on this site also has a **Copy prompt** button that asks your agent to add that example.

## Install the skill

The same file installs as a skill, so your agent knows the table before you ask:

```bash
npx skills add Monabbir-Ahmmad/shadcn-react-table
```

## Registry address

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/r/data-table.json
```

The same address works in Radix UI and Base UI projects; the shadcn CLI adapts the source. Languages are separate items: `…/r/data-table-locale-de.json`. To install by name, register the namespace once in `components.json` (see [Installation](/docs/installation#use-a-namespace-optional)):

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@shadcn-react-table": "https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

## MCP

The shadcn MCP server lets an agent browse and install from the registries in your `components.json`. Register the namespace above, then set up your client:

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest mcp init --client claude   # or cursor, vscode, codex, opencode
```

The agent can then find and add `@shadcn-react-table/data-table` and its languages.

For `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` when the skill isn't installed:

```markdown
## Data table
- components/ui/data-table is shadcn-react-table (installed from its shadcn registry; edit freely).
- Before changing table options read https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/api/use-data-table.md;
  column options: https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/api/column-options.md.
- Pass `getRowId`, and keep `data` and `columns` stable (useMemo, useState or module scope).
- Table-specific column options go in `meta`; state goes through `initialState` / `state` + `on…Change`.
- Reinstall: pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/r/data-table.json --overwrite
  (replaces local edits in components/ui/data-table).
```

# Quick start

A minimal table is two pieces: **columns** (TanStack column defs, typed with `DataTableColumnDef`) and a call to **`useDataTable`**, whose result you hand to **`<DataTable />`**.

```tsx
"use client"

import * as React from "react"
import {
  DataTable,
  useDataTable,
  type DataTableColumnDef,
} from "@/components/ui/data-table"

type Person = { id: string; name: string; email: string; age: number }

const data: Person[] = [
  { id: "1", name: "Ada Lovelace", email: "ada@example.com", age: 36 },
  { id: "2", name: "Alan Turing", email: "alan@example.com", age: 41 },
  { id: "3", name: "Grace Hopper", email: "grace@example.com", age: 85 },
]

const columns: DataTableColumnDef<Person>[] = [
  { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
  { accessorKey: "email", header: "Email" },
  { accessorKey: "age", header: "Age", meta: { align: "right" } },
]

export function PeopleTable() {
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })

  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

That already gives you sorting, client pagination, a toolbar with global search, column visibility, and density controls:

Example (`basic`):

```tsx
function BasicExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

## Turning features on

Every feature is an option on `useDataTable`. Flip a flag to enable it — for example, multi-column sorting, per-column filters, and row selection:

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableMultiSort: true,
  initialState: { showColumnFilters: true },
  enableRowSelection: true,
})
```

> **Memoize data and columns:** Pass stable references for `data` and `columns` (e.g. via `React.useMemo` or
>   module scope). Handing TanStack a new `columns` identity every render can
>   reset state.

## Where to go next

- [Usage](/docs/usage) — the options-in / instance-out model and `table.dataTable`.
- [Guides](/docs/guides/sorting) — enable each feature, with live examples.
- [API reference](/docs/api/use-data-table) — every option and its default.

# Usage

The data table has one core idea: **options in, instance out.**

```tsx
const table = useDataTable(options) // enriched TanStack instance
return <DataTable table={table} /> // renders it
```

## The hook

`useDataTable(options)` wraps TanStack's `useTable`. It:

- supplies default row models (core, sorted, filtered, faceted, grouped, expanded, paginated) — TanStack v9 no longer accepts row-model options, so the table wires them itself;
- injects display columns when needed (selection, row numbers, drag handle, expand, row actions);
- merges localization and icons (built-in defaults → [`DataTableConfigProvider`](/docs/guides/custom-icons) → per-call options);
- adds to the instance: UI state in **`table.getState()`**, methods such as **`table.setDensity`**, and the resolved options on **`table.dataTable`**.

Because it extends TanStack's `TableOptions`, **anything TanStack accepts passes through**: controlled `state`, `on*Change` handlers, `manual*` server-side flags, `getRowId`, `getSubRows`, `initialState`, and so on.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  // data-table options
  enableGrouping: true,
  // standard TanStack options, passed straight through
  state: { sorting },
  onSortingChange: setSorting,
  manualPagination: true,
  rowCount: total,
})
```

## The component

`<DataTable table={table} />` reads `table.dataTable` and renders the full layout: top toolbar → alert banner → drop-to-group zone → bordered scroll surface (sticky header, optional filter row, body, optional sticky footer) → pagination.

Any extra `div` props land on its root — see [DataTable props](/docs/api/data-table-props). To style or add props to an inner part, such as bounding the scroll surface for sticky headers or virtualization, use [`slotProps`](/docs/guides/slot-props):

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  slotProps: { surface: { className: "max-h-[600px]" } },
})
```

## The instance

The table's parts read their configuration from the instance rather than via props. You can use it too — for toolbar actions, custom layouts, or programmatic control:

```tsx
renderTopToolbarCustomActions: ({ table }) => (
  <Button onClick={() => table.beginCreate()}>New row</Button>
)
```

The UI state (density, full screen, filter visibility, editing…) is in `table.getState()`, its methods are on `table` (`setDensity`, `beginRowEdit`, `cancelEdit`, …), and every resolved option and DOM ref is on `table.dataTable`. See the full [Table instance](/docs/api/table-instance) reference.

## Columns

Columns are TanStack column defs, typed with `DataTableColumnDef`. The table reads extra per-column configuration from **`columnDef.meta`** — filter variant, alignment, edit variant, aggregation labels, click-to-copy, and more. See [Column options](/docs/api/column-options).

```tsx
const columns: DataTableColumnDef<Person>[] = [
  {
    accessorKey: "status",
    header: "Status",
    meta: {
      filterVariant: "multi-select",
      filterSelectOptions: STATUS_OPTIONS,
    },
  },
  {
    accessorKey: "salary",
    header: "Salary",
    aggregationFn: "sum",
    meta: {
      align: "right",
      filterVariant: "range-slider",
      editVariant: "number",
    },
  },
]
```

## App-wide defaults

Wrap a subtree in `DataTableConfigProvider` to set default `icons` and `localization` for every table inside it, without editing each call site:

```tsx
import { DataTableConfigProvider } from "@/components/ui/data-table"

;<DataTableConfigProvider localization={spanish} icons={lucideIcons}>
  <App />
</DataTableConfigProvider>
```

Precedence is: built-in defaults → provider → per-call `useDataTable({ localization, icons })`.

# Updating your copy

`shadcn add` copies this block's source into your project — after that,
the code is yours, and upstream releases don't reach it automatically.
This page is the manual update path.

## Know what you have

Every release stamps its version into the registry item. When you
install, note the `meta.version` of
[`/r/data-table.json`](/r/data-table.json) somewhere in your project
(a comment, your PR description). The
[changelog](https://github.com/Monabbir-Ahmmad/shadcn-react-table/blob/main/packages/shadcn-react-table/CHANGELOG.md)
lists what changed in each version.

## Update recipe

1. Start from a clean branch.
2. Re-run the install command with `--overwrite`:

   ```bash
   npx shadcn@latest add --overwrite <registry-url>/r/data-table.json
   ```

3. Review the diff. Everything under `components/ui/data-table/` is
   replaced with the new upstream source — `git diff` shows upstream
   changes mixed with the loss of any local edits you made.
4. Re-apply your local edits on top, or cherry-pick hunks with
   `git checkout -p` against the pre-update commit.
5. Check the changelog for entries marked as breaking and adjust your
   usage.

> **Keep local edits separate:** The less you edit the copied files directly — prefer wrapping the table or
>   using the many `render*` slots — the closer step 3's diff is to a pure
>   upstream update.

## Localization keys and installed locales

When a release adds localization keys, re-add every locale you installed,
otherwise its typecheck fails on the missing keys:

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add --overwrite <registry-url>/r/data-table-locale-de.json
```

Do this after re-adding the table, and re-apply any edits you made to a locale
file.

## Upgrading to 1.0.0

1.0.0 moves the engine to TanStack Table v9 and settles the API. Re-add the block, then:

1. **Type columns with `DataTableColumnDef`.** TanStack v9's `ColumnDef` needs a
   feature-set type parameter; ours supplies it.

   ```ts
   import type { DataTableColumnDef } from "@/components/ui/data-table"
   const columns: DataTableColumnDef<Person>[] = [...]
   ```

   `DataTableRow`, `DataTableColumn`, `DataTableCell`, and `DataTableHeader` are
   the matching instance types. Install `@tanstack/react-table@^9` and
   `@tanstack/match-sorter-utils@^9` (the registry item pins both).

2. **Drop row-model options.** `getCoreRowModel`, `getSortedRowModel`, … are no
   longer accepted; the table wires every row model itself.
3. **Custom aggregation functions** use TanStack v9's
   `constructAggregationFn({ aggregate })` shape. Built-in names (`"sum"`,
   `"mean"`, …) are unchanged.
4. **Instance APIs follow TanStack v9:** `column.pin("start" | "end")`,
   `column.getIsPinned()` returns `"start" | "end"`, `getPrePaginatedRowModel()`.
   Table options and `table.getState()` keep the `left`/`right` pinning shape,
   and `table.getState().columnSizingInfo` keeps its name. Other renames:
   `getLeft*`/`getRight*` are `getStart*`/`getEnd*` (leaf columns, visible
   cells, header groups, total size), `column.getStart("left")` and
   `column.getAfter("right")` take `"start"` / `"end"`, and
   `getPaginationRowModel()` is `getPaginatedRowModel()`.
5. **Option and column-def renames reach you too.** The column option
   `sortingFn` is now `sortFn`. `state.columnSizingInfo`,
   `initialState.columnSizingInfo` and `onColumnSizingInfoChange` are now
   `columnResizing` and `onColumnResizingChange` (only the value returned by
   `table.getState()` keeps the `columnSizingInfo` name).
6. **`filterFns`, `sortingFns` and `aggregationFns` options are gone.** The hook
   owns the feature set, so pass custom functions inline on the column
   (`filterFn: myFilterFn`, `sortFn: myCompare`, `aggregationFn: myAgg`). Built-in
   string names still work. Type inline filter functions with the exported
   `DataTableFilterFn<TData>`.
7. **Don't destructure row/column/cell methods** (`const { getValue } = row`); call
   them on the object. Cell-renderer `({ getValue })` still works.
8. **Row data must satisfy TanStack's `RowData`** (`Record<string, any> | Array<any>`).
   `unknown` is no longer accepted, so use a concrete row type for
   `useDataTable<TData>` and `DataTableInstance<TData>`. `DataTableInstance`
   with no type argument now defaults to `RowData`.
9. **Render contexts are unchanged.** Column renderers (`cell`, `header`,
   `footer`, `aggregatedCell`) still receive the enriched instance, so
   `({ table }) => table.getState()`, `table.dataTable` and the table's
   methods type-check. TanStack v9's own contexts don't include `getState`.
10. **`table.options` is the options object you passed in** on the latest render
    (TanStack v9's React adapter behavior), not TanStack's internally merged
    options with feature defaults.
11. **Two small TanStack features are registered by the block.** Their types
    add `dataTableInstanceFeature` and `dataTableUiFeature` through TanStack's
    `Plugins` / `Table_FeatureMap` / `TableState_FeatureMap` interfaces, scoped
    to tables built with the block's feature set. Other TanStack tables in
    your app are unaffected, except ones typed `Table<any, …>`.
12. **The component holding the table no longer re-renders on table state
    changes.** If it reads the state while rendering (a selection count, the
    current density), add `stateSelector` for what it reads, or wrap that part
    in `table.Subscribe`. See
    [State management](/docs/guides/state#reading-state-in-your-component).

### API renames in 1.0.0

| 0.x                                                                                        | 1.0.0                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table.tableInstance.setDensity(…)` (and every setter or action)                           | `table.setDensity(…)`                                          |
| `table.tableInstance.density` (and other UI state)                                         | `table.getState().density`                                     |
| `table.tableInstance.isLoading` (and other options, `refs`)                                | `table.dataTable.isLoading`                                    |
| `DataTableConfig` type                                                                     | `DataTableOptionsResolved` (+ `DataTableMethods`)              |
| `defaultDensity: "compact"`                                                                | `initialState: { density: "compact" }`                         |
| `density`, `isFullscreen`, `showColumnFilters`, `advancedFilter`, `globalFilterMode` props | `state: { … }`                                                 |
| `defaultShowColumnFilters`, `defaultGlobalFilterMode`, `defaultAdvancedFilter`             | `initialState: { … }`                                          |
| `onEditCellSave` / `onSaveRow` / `onCreateRow`                                             | `onEditingCellSave` / `onEditingRowSave` / `onCreatingRowSave` |
| `renderToolbarActions`                                                                     | `renderTopToolbarCustomActions`                                |
| `meta.variant` / `meta.options`                                                            | `meta.filterVariant` / `meta.filterSelectOptions`              |
| `meta.disableHighlight: true`                                                              | `meta.enableFilterMatchHighlighting: false`                    |
| `meta.disableColumnActions: true`                                                          | `meta.enableColumnActions: false`                              |
| `<DataTable pageSizeOptions={…} />`                                                        | `useDataTable({ pageSizeOptions: … })`                         |
| `<DataTable surfaceClassName="…" />`                                                       | `useDataTable({ slotProps: { surface: { className: "…" } } })` |
| `renderColumnActionsMenuItems` appended after a separator                                   | return `<>{internalMenuItems}<DropdownMenuSeparator />{yours}</>` |
| Edit button next to the `renderRowActionMenuItems` menu                                   | Edit is in the menu: render `internalMenuItems` in your items     |
| `sortingFns` option                                                                         | `sortFns`                                                          |

## Related

- [Installation](/docs/installation)

# Migrating from Material React Table

The data table follows Material React Table (MRT) closely: the same hook-then-component shape, most of the same options, and the same TanStack Table underneath. Moving a table over is mostly renaming. This page lists what changes.

## The basics

```tsx
// Material React Table
const table = useMaterialReactTable({ columns, data })
return <MaterialReactTable table={table} />

// This data table
const table = useDataTable({ columns, data, getRowId: (row) => row.id })
return <DataTable table={table} />
```

- Type columns with `DataTableColumnDef<TData>` instead of `MRT_ColumnDef<TData>`.
- Pass `getRowId` — row selection, editing and pinning key rows by id.
- The table runs on **TanStack Table v9**, MRT on v8. The column options you share with TanStack (`accessorKey`, `cell`, `header`, `footer`, `sortFn`, `filterFn`, `enableSorting`, …) keep TanStack's names; v9 renames a few v8 ones, such as `sortingFn` → `sortFn`.

## Column options

MRT puts its own column options on the column definition. Here they live under `meta`.

| MRT column option | Here |
| --- | --- |
| `Cell` / `Header` / `Footer` | `cell` / `header` / `footer` (TanStack's) |
| `filterVariant` | `meta.filterVariant` |
| `filterSelectOptions` | `meta.filterSelectOptions` |
| `filterFn` (a mode name) | `meta.filterMode` |
| `columnFilterModeOptions` | `meta.columnFilterModeOptions` |
| `enableColumnFilterModes` | `meta.enableColumnFilterModes` |
| `Filter` | `meta.renderColumnFilter` |
| `editVariant` / `editSelectOptions` | `meta.editVariant` / `meta.editSelectOptions` |
| `enableEditing` | `meta.enableEditing` |
| `Edit` | `meta.renderEditCell` |
| `muiEditTextFieldProps` validation | `meta.validate` (return a message to block the save) |
| `GroupedCell` / `AggregatedCell` / `PlaceholderCell` | `meta.renderGroupedCell` / `meta.renderAggregatedCell` / `meta.renderPlaceholderCell` |
| `enableClickToCopy` | `meta.enableClickToCopy` |
| `enableColumnActions` | `meta.enableColumnActions` |
| `visibleInShowHideMenu` | `meta.visibleInShowHideMenu` |
| `muiTableHeadCellProps` / `muiTableBodyCellProps` / `muiTableFooterCellProps` | `meta.slotProps.headCell` / `.bodyCell` / `.footerCell` |

## Component props (`mui*Props`)

MRT's `mui*Props` become one `slotProps` option. Each part takes props or a function of its context, and merges them with the table's own. See [Part props](/docs/guides/slot-props).

| MRT | `slotProps` part |
| --- | --- |
| `muiTablePaperProps` | `root` |
| `muiTableContainerProps` | `surface` |
| `muiTableProps` | `table` |
| `muiTableHeadProps` / `muiTableHeadRowProps` / `muiTableHeadCellProps` | `head` / `headRow` / `headCell` |
| `muiFilterTextFieldProps` (cell) | `filterCell` |
| `muiTableBodyProps` / `muiTableBodyRowProps` / `muiTableBodyCellProps` | `body` / `bodyRow` / `bodyCell` |
| `muiDetailPanelProps` | `detailPanel` |
| `muiTableFooterProps` / `muiTableFooterRowProps` / `muiTableFooterCellProps` | `footer` / `footerRow` / `footerCell` |
| `muiTopToolbarProps` / `muiBottomToolbarProps` | `topToolbar` / `bottomToolbar` |
| `muiPaginationProps` | `pagination` |
| `muiToolbarAlertBannerProps` | `alertBanner` |
| `muiSearchTextFieldProps` | `searchInput` |
| `muiEditTextFieldProps` | `editField` |
| `muiEditRowDialogProps` / `muiCreateRowModalProps` | `editDialog` (`isCreating` tells them apart) |
| `muiSelectCheckboxProps` | `selectCheckbox` |

## State

| MRT state | Here |
| --- | --- |
| `isFullScreen` | `isFullscreen` |
| `columnFilterFns` | `columnFilterModes` |
| `globalFilterFn` | `globalFilterMode` |
| `editingRow` | `editingRowId` (the draft is in `rowDraft`) |
| `editingCell` | `editingCell` (`{ rowId, columnId }`) |
| `creatingRow` | `isCreating` (the draft is in `rowDraft`) |
| `isLoading` / `isSaving` / `showProgressBars` / `showSkeletons` / `showLoadingOverlay` | options of the same names, not state |
| `density`, `showColumnFilters`, and TanStack's own state | unchanged |

Set and control state the same way: `initialState`, `state`, and the matching `on…Change` callback (`onIsFullScreenChange` → `onIsFullscreenChange`, `onColumnFilterFnsChange` → `onColumnFilterModesChange`, `onGlobalFilterFnChange` → `onGlobalFilterModeChange`). See [State management](/docs/guides/state).

## Table options

Most options keep their MRT names: `enableRowSelection`, `enableMultiRowSelection`, `enableBatchRowSelection`, `enableSelectAll`, `selectAllMode`, `enableEditing`, `editDisplayMode`, `createDisplayMode`, `positionCreatingRow`, `enableGrouping`, `enableColumnPinning`, `enableRowPinning`, `enableColumnOrdering`, `enableColumnResizing`, `enableRowOrdering`, `enableRowNumbers`, `enableRowVirtualization`, `enableColumnVirtualization`, `rowVirtualizerOptions`, `columnVirtualizerOptions`, `enableStickyHeader`, `enableStickyFooter`, `enableTableHead`, `enableTableFooter`, `enableExpandAll`, `enableColumnFilterModes`, `enableGlobalFilterModes`, `enableGlobalFilterRankedResults`, `enableFacetedValues`, `enableFilterMatchHighlighting`, `enableClickToCopy`, `enableCellActions`, `enableDensityToggle`, `enableFullScreenToggle` → `enableFullscreenToggle`, `enableTopToolbar`, `enableBottomToolbar`, `enableToolbarInternalActions`, `columnFilterDisplayMode`, `paginationDisplayMode`, `positionPagination`, `positionGlobalFilter`, `positionActionsColumn`, `positionExpandColumn`, `positionToolbarAlertBanner`, `positionToolbarDropZone`, `displayColumnDefOptions`, `defaultDisplayColumn`, `filterFns`, `aggregationFns`, `columnFilterModeOptions`, `globalFilterModeOptions`, `localization`, `icons`.

Renamed or reshaped:

| MRT | Here |
| --- | --- |
| `sortingFns` | `sortFns` (TanStack v9's name) |
| `rowNumberDisplayMode` | `rowNumberMode` |
| `renderEmptyRowsFallback` | `renderEmpty` |
| `muiPaginationProps.rowsPerPageOptions` | `pageSizeOptions` |
| `state.isLoading` and friends | the `isLoading`, `isSaving`, `showProgressBars`, `showSkeletons`, `showLoadingOverlay` options |
| `onEditingRowSave({ values, table })`, then `table.setEditingRow(null)` | `onEditingRowSave({ row, values, table, exit })`, then `exit()` |
| `onCreatingRowSave({ values, table })`, then `table.setCreatingRow(null)` | `onCreatingRowSave({ values, table, exit })`, then `exit()` |
| cell edits saved from `muiEditTextFieldProps.onBlur` | `onEditingCellSave({ row, column, value, table })` |
| `displayColumnDefOptions["mrt-row-select"]` (and the other `mrt-row-*` ids) | `displayColumnDefOptions["cn-select"]` — ids: `cn-select`, `cn-expand`, `cn-row-actions`, `cn-row-number`, `cn-row-pin`, `cn-row-drag` |

Callbacks and render options with the same name and arguments: `onEditingRowCancel`, `onCreatingRowCancel`, `renderTopToolbarCustomActions`, `renderBottomToolbarCustomActions`, `renderToolbarInternalActions`, `renderTopToolbar`, `renderBottomToolbar`, `renderRowActions`, `renderDetailPanel`, `renderCaption`, `renderEditRowDialogContent`, `renderCreateRowDialogContent`, `renderColumnFilterModeMenuItems`, `renderGlobalFilterModeMenuItems`, and the menu callbacks `renderColumnActionsMenuItems`, `renderRowActionMenuItems`, `renderCellActionMenuItems` (each receives `internalMenuItems` and `closeMenu`).

## The table instance

| MRT | Here |
| --- | --- |
| `table.setEditingRow(row)` | `table.beginRowEdit(row)` |
| `table.setEditingRow(null)` / `table.setCreatingRow(null)` | `table.cancelEdit()` |
| `table.setCreatingRow(true)` | `table.beginCreate()` |
| `table.setEditingCell(cell)` | `table.setEditingCell({ rowId, columnId })` |
| `table.setIsFullScreen(…)` | `table.setIsFullscreen(…)` |
| `table.setColumnFilterFns(…)` | `table.setColumnFilterMode(columnId, mode)` |
| `table.setGlobalFilterFn(…)` | `table.setGlobalFilterMode(mode)` |
| `table.refs.tableContainerRef` (and the other refs) | `table.dataTable.refs.tableContainerRef` |
| `table.options.enableEditing` (and MRT's other options) | `table.dataTable.enableEditing` |
| `table.getState()` | unchanged, including the UI state above |

The instance is stable and the component that calls `useDataTable` does not re-render on state changes. Read state where you render it with `table.Subscribe`, or pass `stateSelector`. See [State management](/docs/guides/state).

## Defaults that differ

| Option | MRT | Here | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `editDisplayMode` | `"modal"` | `"cell"` | Inline editing is the quickest edit for most tables |
| `positionActionsColumn` | `"first"` | `"last"` | Actions read best after the data they act on |
| `enableStickyHeader` | `false` | `true` | Headers stay useful on long tables |
| `enableFacetedValues` | `false` | `true` | Select filters fill their options from the data |
| `enableGlobalFilterRankedResults` | `true` | `false` | Searching never reorders rows unless you opt in |
| Text filter mode | `"fuzzy"` | `"contains"` | Predictable matches; fuzzy is one menu click away |
| Cell editing starts on | double-click | single click | One click to edit, matching the click-to-edit affordance |

Set the MRT value explicitly to keep the old behavior.

## Not here (yet)

- `layoutMode` and column `grow`, and the `"head-overlay"` alert banner position.
- `rowPinningDisplayMode` values `"sticky"` and `"select-sticky"` (rows that stick in place); use `"top-and-bottom"` or `"select-top"`.
- `enableColumnDragging` as a separate switch.
- MRT's `enableRowDragging` works through `DataTableDndProvider` and `onRowDragEnd` here; see [Row dragging](/docs/guides/row-dragging).
- MUI theming: the table uses your shadcn/ui components and theme instead.

## Related

- [Updating](/docs/guides/updating)
- [Part props (slotProps)](/docs/guides/slot-props)
- [State management](/docs/guides/state)

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/column-filtering/ -->

# Column filtering

Each column can expose its own filter control in a per-column filter row. Toggle the row with the funnel icon in the toolbar, or have it open from the start with `initialState: { showColumnFilters: true }`.

Example (`column-filters`):

```tsx
function ColumnFiltersExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    initialState: { showColumnFilters: true, pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

## Choosing a filter control

The UI for each filter is chosen by the column's `meta.filterVariant`:

| Variant | Control | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"text"` (default) | Text box | Any |
| `"autocomplete"` | Text box suggesting the column's values | Any |
| `"select"` / `"multi-select"` | Dropdown / checklist | Strings |
| `"checkbox"` | Checkbox | Booleans |
| `"range"` / `"range-slider"` | Number boxes / slider | Numbers |
| `"date"` / `"date-range"` | Calendar | Dates, compared by day |
| `"datetime"` / `"datetime-range"` | Date-time box | Dates, compared to the minute |
| `"time"` / `"time-range"` | Time box | `"HH:mm"` strings or Dates, compared by time of day |

The date, date-time and time variants share the same modes (equals, before, after, between, empty…); the `-range` variants start in "between".

For `select`, `multi-select` and `autocomplete`, supply `meta.filterSelectOptions` as an array of `{ label, value }`. If you omit them, the options are derived from the column's faceted unique values.

```tsx
import { DataTable, useDataTable } from "@/components/ui/data-table"

const columns = [
  { accessorKey: "title", header: "Title", meta: { filterVariant: "text" } },
  {
    accessorKey: "status",
    header: "Status",
    meta: {
      filterVariant: "select",
      filterSelectOptions: [
        { label: "Active", value: "active" },
        { label: "Archived", value: "archived" },
      ],
    },
  },
  { accessorKey: "score", header: "Score", meta: { filterVariant: "range" } },
]

const table = useDataTable({ data, columns, getRowId: (row) => row.id })
return <DataTable table={table} />
```

Example (`datetime-filters`):

```tsx
function DateTimeFiltersExample() {
  const table = useDataTable({
    data: SHIFTS,
    columns: SHIFT_COLUMNS,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    initialState: { showColumnFilters: true, pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

## Open the filter row by default

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  initialState: { showColumnFilters: true },
})
```

## Custom filter UI

Use `meta.renderColumnFilter` as an escape hatch to render your own filter control for a column.

## Match highlighting

Matched substrings in cells are highlighted by default. Disable it for the whole table with `enableFilterMatchHighlighting: false`, or for a single column with `meta.enableFilterMatchHighlighting: true`.

## Disabling a column's filter

Set `enableColumnFilter: false` on a column to remove its filter control entirely.

## Faceted values

Select / multi-select filters auto-derive their options, and range filters their min/max bounds, from the data's faceted values. This is on by default; set `enableFacetedValues: false` to skip computing the faceted row models (e.g. for very large client-side datasets) — then provide `meta.filterSelectOptions` explicitly for select-style filters.

## Relevant options

`useDataTable` options that affect column filtering:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onShowColumnFiltersChange` | `(showColumnFilters: boolean) => void` |  | Called whenever the filter row is shown or hidden. Set it with `initialState.showColumnFilters`, control it with `state.showColumnFilters`. |
| `enableColumnFilterModes` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the filter-mode menu adornment on filter fields. Default true. |
| `enableFilterMatchHighlighting` | `boolean` | `true` | Highlight matched substrings in cells. Default true. |
| `enableFacetedValues` | `boolean` | `true` | Compute faceted unique values / min-max (auto select options + range bounds). Default true; disable to skip the faceted row models. |
| `columnFilterDisplayMode` | `ColumnFilterDisplayMode` | `"subheader"` | Where column filter inputs live: `"subheader"` (a filter row under the header, default), `"popover"` (per-column popovers opened from the column header), or `"custom"` (you render them). |

Per-column, via `columnDef.meta`:

| meta key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filterVariant` | `FilterVariant` |  | Filter UI variant rendered in the filter row. Defaults to "text". |
| `filterSelectOptions` | `DataTableFilterOption[]` |  | Options for `select` / `multi-select` filter variants. If omitted for a select-style variant, options are derived from faceted unique values. |
| `filterMode` | `FilterMode` |  | Default filter mode for this column (overrides the per-variant default). |
| `enableColumnFilterModes` | `boolean` |  | Per-column override for the filter-mode menu (defaults to the table). |
| `renderColumnFilter` | `(props: { column: Column<TFeatures, TData, TValue> table: DataTableInstance<TData> }) => React.ReactNode` |  | Custom filter UI for this column (escape hatch). Replaces the variant. |
| `columnFilterModeOptions` | `FilterMode[]` |  | Restrict (and order) the filter-mode menu for this column to this subset of modes (built-in ones and custom `filterFns` names). Include the column's default mode. |
| `enableFilterMatchHighlighting` | `boolean` |  | `false` opts this column out of match highlighting (the table option of the same name turns it on or off for every column). |

## Related

- [Filter modes](/docs/guides/filter-modes)
- [Display modes](/docs/guides/display-modes)
- [Column options](/docs/api/column-options)

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/filter-modes/ -->

# Filter modes

Filter modes let users change how a column's filter is applied — for example matching with Contains, Starts with, Equals, Between, Greater than, or Empty. With `enableColumnFilterModes: true` (the default) each filter field shows a mode menu offering the modes appropriate to that column's `meta.filterVariant`.

Example (`filter-modes`):

```tsx
function FilterModesExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableColumnFilterModes: true,
    initialState: { showColumnFilters: true, pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

## Setting the initial mode

Set a column's starting mode with `meta.filterMode`.

```tsx
import { DataTable, useDataTable } from "@/components/ui/data-table"

const columns = [
  {
    accessorKey: "title",
    header: "Title",
    meta: { filterVariant: "text", filterMode: "startsWith" },
  },
  {
    accessorKey: "score",
    header: "Score",
    meta: { filterVariant: "range", filterMode: "between" },
  },
]

const table = useDataTable({ data, columns, getRowId: (row) => row.id })
return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## Toggling the mode menu

`enableColumnFilterModes` is `true` by default. Turn it off globally to hide every mode menu, or override it per column with `meta.enableColumnFilterModes`.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableColumnFilterModes: false,
})
```

```tsx
const columns = [
  // mode menu hidden for this column only
  { accessorKey: "id", header: "ID", meta: { enableColumnFilterModes: false } },
]
```

## Restricting the available modes

Limit a column's mode menu to a specific subset (and order) with `meta.columnFilterModeOptions`. Only modes valid for the column's variant are kept (plus any [custom functions](#custom-filter-functions)); include the column's default mode.

```tsx
const columns = [
  {
    accessorKey: "title",
    header: "Title",
    meta: {
      filterVariant: "text",
      filterMode: "contains",
      columnFilterModeOptions: ["contains", "startsWith", "equals"],
    },
  },
]
```

To restrict every column at once, pass `columnFilterModeOptions` to `useDataTable`. Each column keeps the modes its variant supports; a column's own `meta.columnFilterModeOptions` wins.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  columnFilterModeOptions: ["contains", "equals", "between", "betweenInclusive"],
})
```

## Custom filter functions

Add your own filter functions with the `filterFns` option. Each one takes TanStack's filter function arguments — `(row, columnId, filterValue)` — and returns whether the row passes. Then use it by name:

- in a mode menu, by listing it in `meta.columnFilterModeOptions` or `columnFilterModeOptions`;
- as a column's starting mode, with `meta.filterMode`;
- as a column's fixed filter (no mode menu), with `filterFn`;
- in the global search, by listing it in `globalFilterModeOptions` — see [Global search](/docs/guides/global-search#custom-search-modes).

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns: [
    {
      accessorKey: "name",
      header: "Name",
      meta: {
        columnFilterModeOptions: ["contains", "startsWith", "wordStartsWith"],
      },
    },
  ],
  filterFns: {
    wordStartsWith: (row, columnId, value) =>
      String(row.getValue(columnId))
        .toLowerCase()
        .split(/\s+/)
        .some((word) => word.startsWith(String(value).toLowerCase())),
  },
  localization: { filterModes: { wordStartsWith: "Any word starts with" } },
})
```

The menu labels a custom function with `localization.filterModes[name]`, or the name itself when there is no label. The names are read when the table is created, so define the functions outside your component (or memoize them).

Example (`custom-filter-fns`):

```tsx
function CustomFilterFnsExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns: NAME_COLUMNS,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    initialState: {
      showColumnFilters: true,
      pagination: { pageSize: 10 },
    },
    // Matches when any word of the cell starts with the typed text.
    filterFns: {
      wordStartsWith: (row, columnId, value) =>
        String(row.getValue(columnId))
          .toLowerCase()
          .split(/\s+/)
          .some((word) => word.startsWith(String(value).toLowerCase())),
    },
    localization: { filterModes: { wordStartsWith: "Any word starts with" } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

## Custom mode menu

Replace the built-in radio items with your own using `renderColumnFilterModeMenuItems`. You get the allowed `modes`, the `currentMode`, and an `onSelect(mode)` to switch.

```tsx
import { DropdownMenuItem } from "@/components/ui/dropdown-menu"

const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  renderColumnFilterModeMenuItems: ({ modes, currentMode, onSelect }) =>
    modes.map((mode) => (
      <DropdownMenuItem
        key={mode}
        disabled={mode === currentMode}
        onClick={() => onSelect(mode)}
      >
        {mode}
      </DropdownMenuItem>
    )),
})
```

The global-search mode menu has the same hook: `renderGlobalFilterModeMenuItems` — see [Global search](/docs/guides/global-search).

## Localizing mode labels

Mode menu labels are localizable via `localization.filterModes`. Labels you pass are merged with the built-in ones, so you only need to list the modes you change or add.

## Related

- [Column filtering](/docs/guides/column-filtering)
- [Localization](/docs/api/localization)

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/global-search/ -->

# Global search

An expandable global search box appears in the toolbar by default (`enableGlobalFilter: true`). It filters across all searchable columns at once, complementing the per-column filters.

Example (`global-search`):

```tsx
function GlobalSearchExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableGlobalFilter: true,
    initialState: { globalFilterMode: "fuzzy", pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

## Search modes

When `enableGlobalFilterModes: true` (the default), the search box shows a mode menu — fuzzy, contains, and more. The initial mode comes from `initialState.globalFilterMode`, which defaults to `"fuzzy"`.

```tsx
import { DataTable, useDataTable } from "@/components/ui/data-table"

const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableGlobalFilter: true,
  enableGlobalFilterModes: true,
  initialState: { globalFilterMode: "fuzzy" },
})
return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## Opening the search box

The search box starts closed (a search button) unless a search is set. Its open state is table state, `showGlobalFilter`: start it open with `initialState: { showGlobalFilter: true }`, control it with `state.showGlobalFilter` and `onShowGlobalFilterChange`, or open it from code with `table.setShowGlobalFilter(true)`. Setting a search value from outside opens it too.

## Custom search modes

Limit or reorder the search mode menu with `globalFilterModeOptions`. It can also list your own [custom filter functions](/docs/guides/filter-modes#custom-filter-functions) by name; the search runs them on each searchable column, and a row matches when any column passes.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  filterFns: {
    exact: (row, columnId, value) => String(row.getValue(columnId)) === value,
  },
  globalFilterModeOptions: ["contains", "fuzzy", "exact"],
  initialState: { globalFilterMode: "contains" },
  localization: { filterModes: { exact: "Exact match" } },
})
```

## Disabling global search

Set `enableGlobalFilter: false` to remove the search box from the toolbar.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableGlobalFilter: false,
})
```

## Custom mode menu

Replace the built-in mode radio items with `renderGlobalFilterModeMenuItems`. It receives the allowed `modes`, the `currentMode`, and an `onSelect(mode)` to switch.

```tsx
import { DropdownMenuItem } from "@/components/ui/dropdown-menu"

useDataTable({
  renderGlobalFilterModeMenuItems: ({ modes, currentMode, onSelect }) =>
    modes.map((mode) => (
      <DropdownMenuItem
        key={mode}
        disabled={mode === currentMode}
        onClick={() => onSelect(mode)}
      >
        {mode}
      </DropdownMenuItem>
    )),
})
```

## Ranked results

In fuzzy mode, each match carries a relevance score. Set `enableGlobalFilterRankedResults` to order rows by that score — best matches first — for as long as a search is active.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  initialState: { globalFilterMode: "fuzzy" },
  enableGlobalFilterRankedResults: true,
})
```

The ranking yields to the user: the moment they click a column to sort, their sort takes over, and clearing the search restores the original order. It applies only in `"fuzzy"` mode and is skipped while grouping or row expansion is active, or under `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` (the server owns ordering there).

> **Off by default:** Material React Table enables this by default; the data table keeps it off so adding a
>   search box never silently reorders your rows. Opt in when relevance ordering
>   is what you want.

## Placement

Move the search to the left toolbar region with `positionGlobalFilter: "left"` — see [Toolbar customization](/docs/guides/toolbar#search-placement).

## Relevant options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enableGlobalFilter` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the expandable global search in the toolbar. Default true. |
| `enableGlobalFilterModes` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the global search mode menu (fuzzy/contains/…). Default true. |
| `onShowGlobalFilterChange` | `(showGlobalFilter: boolean) => void` |  | Called whenever the global search box opens or closes. Set it with `initialState.showGlobalFilter`, control it with `state.showGlobalFilter`. |
| `globalFilterModeOptions` | `GlobalFilterMode[]` | `GLOBAL_FILTER_MODES as GlobalFilterMode[]` | Restrict (and order) the global search mode menu: built-in modes and custom `filterFns` names. |
| `enableGlobalFilterRankedResults` | `boolean` | `false` | While the global search is in fuzzy mode, order rows by best match (most relevant first) until the user applies their own sort. Default false — MRT defaults this on, but the data table keeps it off so searching never silently reorders rows unless opted in. Ignored for non-fuzzy modes, when grouping or expanded, or under manual sorting/filtering. |
| `onGlobalFilterModeChange` | `(mode: GlobalFilterMode) => void` |  | Called whenever the global search mode changes (default `"fuzzy"`). Set it with `initialState.globalFilterMode`, control it with `state.globalFilterMode`. |
| `positionGlobalFilter` | `"left" \| "right" \| "none"` | `"right"` | Which toolbar region the global search renders in. Default "right" (the internal-actions cluster). "left" places it next to the title/actions; "none" hides it (same as `enableGlobalFilter: false`). |

## Related

- [Column filtering](/docs/guides/column-filtering)
- [Filter modes](/docs/guides/filter-modes)

---

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/advanced-filter/ -->

# Advanced filter

Set `enableAdvancedFilter: true` to add a toolbar button that opens a dialog where users build compound filter rules — multiple conditions joined by **All** (AND) or **Any** (OR) logic. The button badges the number of active rules.

Example (`advanced-filter`):

```tsx
function AdvancedFilterExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableAdvancedFilter: true,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableAdvancedFilter: true,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## How it works

Each rule is a `{ columnId, operator, value }`. The available operators adapt to the column's `meta.filterVariant`:

| Variant                   | Operators                                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text` (default)          | contains, does not contain, starts with, ends with, equals, not equals, is empty, is not empty |
| `select` / `multi-select` | equals, not equals, is empty, is not empty                                                     |
| `range` / `range-slider`  | equals, not equals, `>`, `≥`, `<`, `≤`, between, is empty, is not empty                        |
| `date` / `date-range`     | equals, not equals, `>`, `<`, between, is empty, is not empty                                  |
| `checkbox`                | equals                                                                                         |

Build your rules in the dialog, then click **Apply** to filter the table. Closing or cancelling the dialog discards unapplied edits.

> **Additive to column filters:** The advanced filter is independent of the per-column filter row and global
>   search: a row must pass <em>all</em> active filter systems to be shown. Clear
>   the panel's rules (or use "Clear all") to remove just the advanced filters.

## Controlled usage

Drive the filter from your own state with `state.advancedFilter` + `onAdvancedFilterChange` (or seed an uncontrolled table with `initialState.advancedFilter`).

```tsx
const [filter, setFilter] = React.useState<AdvancedFilterGroup>({
  logic: "and",
  rules: [],
})

const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  enableAdvancedFilter: true,
  state: { advancedFilter: filter },
  onAdvancedFilterChange: setFilter,
})
```

## Related

- [Column filtering](/docs/guides/column-filtering)
- [Filter modes](/docs/guides/filter-modes)
- [useDataTable options](/docs/api/use-data-table)

# Column visibility

A "Columns" toggle in the toolbar lets users show or hide columns. Each column-actions menu also has a Hide item for the same effect.

Example (`column-visibility`):

```tsx
function ColumnVisibilityExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    initialState: {
      columnVisibility: { startDate: false, progress: false },
      pagination: { pageSize: 10 },
    },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## Initial hidden columns
Hide columns from the start with `initialState.columnVisibility`, mapping a column id to `false`.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  initialState: {
    columnVisibility: { startDate: false },
  },
})
```

## Prevent hiding a column
Use TanStack's `enableHiding: false` on a column definition to keep it always visible. It will not appear in the toggle or expose a Hide item.

```tsx
const columns = [
  { accessorKey: "firstName", enableHiding: false },
]
```

> **Always-on columns:** Columns with `enableHiding: false` stay rendered regardless of toolbar or menu actions.

## Leaving a column out of the menu

Set `meta.visibleInShowHideMenu: false` to keep a column out of the show / hide columns menu while still letting it be hidden from code (`column.toggleVisibility`).

# Column ordering

Set `enableColumnOrdering: true` to add a drag grip to each header. Users can grab the grip and drag a column to a new position.

Example (`column-ordering`):

```tsx
function ColumnOrderingExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableColumnOrdering: true,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableColumnOrdering: true,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## While you drag

The whole column moves with its header — body, filter and footer cells included — and the other columns slide aside to show where it will land. The movement comes from CSS variables on the scroll surface, so dragging doesn't re-render any rows. With "reduce motion" turned on in the operating system, the columns move without the slide animation.

## Initial order
Provide the starting order with `initialState.columnOrder`, an array of column ids.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  enableColumnOrdering: true,
  initialState: {
    columnOrder: ["firstName", "lastName", "salary"],
  },
})
```

> **Pair with pinning:** Pinned columns stay anchored while the rest reorder. Combine ordering with pinning to keep key columns in view.

## Related
- [Column pinning](/docs/guides/column-pinning)
- [useDataTable options](/docs/api/use-data-table)
- [Column options](/docs/api/column-options)

# Column pinning

Set `enableColumnPinning: true` to let users pin columns left or right from the column-actions menu. Pinned columns stay sticky while the table scrolls horizontally.

Example (`column-pinning`):

```tsx
function ColumnPinningExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableColumnPinning: true,
    initialState: {
      columnPinning: { left: ["firstName"], right: ["salary"] },
      pagination: { pageSize: 10 },
    },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableColumnPinning: true,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## Initial pins
Pin columns from the start with `initialState.columnPinning`, grouping ids into `left` and `right`.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  enableColumnPinning: true,
  initialState: {
    columnPinning: {
      left: ["firstName"],
      right: ["salary"],
    },
  },
})
```

Table options and `table.getState()` use `left` / `right`, while instance methods such as `column.pin` and `column.getIsPinned` use TanStack v9's `start` / `end`.

> **Sticky positioning:** Pinned columns rely on the same sticky behavior used elsewhere in the table. See the sticky guide for how that interacts with headers and footers.

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/column-resizing/ -->

# Column resizing

Set `enableColumnResizing: true` to add a drag handle on each column's edge. Users drag the handle to widen or narrow a column.

Example (`column-resizing`):

```tsx
function ColumnResizingExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableColumnResizing: true,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableColumnResizing: true,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## Keyboard

Each resize handle is focusable. With it focused, the arrow keys widen or narrow the column by 10px (50px with Shift) — mirrored in right-to-left tables — Home and End jump to the column's `minSize` and `maxSize`, and Enter fits the column to its content (or resets it when auto-size is off). Screen readers hear it as a separator with the column's current width.

## Resize mode

The resize mode defaults to `"onChange"`, so columns resize live as the handle moves. Pass TanStack's `columnResizeMode: "onEnd"` to defer the resize until the handle is released.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  enableColumnResizing: true,
  columnResizeMode: "onEnd",
})
```

## Width constraints

Column widths come from `size`, `minSize`, and `maxSize` on the column definition.

```tsx
const columns = [
  { accessorKey: "firstName", size: 200, minSize: 120, maxSize: 320 },
]
```

> **Set sensible bounds:** Define `minSize` and `maxSize` so users cannot collapse or stretch a column
>   past a usable width.

## Auto-sizing

Double-click a column's resize handle to size it to fit its widest value — header and data, across the full dataset (not just the rows currently on screen). This is on by default whenever `enableColumnResizing` is set, and respects each column's `minSize`/`maxSize` bounds.

Set `enableColumnAutosize: false` to turn it off; double-clicking the handle then resets the column to its default size instead.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  enableColumnResizing: true,
  enableColumnAutosize: true, // default: matches enableColumnResizing
})
```

You can also trigger it imperatively from the table instance:

```tsx
table.autoSizeColumn("firstName")
table.autoSizeAllColumns()
```

Example (`column-autosize`):

```tsx
function ColumnAutosizeExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableColumnResizing: true,
    enableColumnAutosize: true,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
    renderTopToolbarCustomActions: ({ table }) => (
      <Button
        size="sm"
        variant="outline"
        onClick={() => table.autoSizeAllColumns()}
      >
        Fit all columns
      </Button>
    ),
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

- [Column options](/docs/api/column-options)
- [useDataTable options](/docs/api/use-data-table)

# Row selection

Set `enableRowSelection: true` to add a leading checkbox column. When rows are selected, a selection alert banner appears showing the current count.

`enableRowSelection` accepts a boolean or a `(row) => boolean` predicate (standard TanStack), so you can allow selecting only certain rows.

> **Stable selection keys:** Always provide `getRowId` so selection keys stay stable across re-renders,
>   sorting, and pagination. Without it, selection is keyed by row index and can
>   drift.

## row-selection

Multi-row selection with a select-all checkbox in the header.

Example (`row-selection`):

```tsx
function RowSelectionExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableRowSelection: true,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableRowSelection: true,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

Read the current selection at any time. To show it in your own component's render, subscribe to it with `stateSelector` (the component holding the table does not re-render on table changes by default; see [State management](/docs/guides/state#reading-state-in-your-component)):

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  // …
  enableRowSelection: true,
  stateSelector: (state) => state.rowSelection,
})

const selected = table.getState().rowSelection
```

Or control it from your own state:

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableRowSelection: true,
  state: { rowSelection },
  onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
})
```

You can also gate selection per row with a predicate:

```tsx
enableRowSelection: (row) => row.original.status !== "archived"
```

## single-selection

For single selection, add `enableMultiRowSelection: false`. The checkboxes become radio buttons and the select-all checkbox goes away.

Example (`single-selection`):

```tsx
function SingleSelectionExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableRowSelection: true,
    enableMultiRowSelection: false,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableRowSelection: true,
  enableMultiRowSelection: false,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## Selecting a range

Click one row's checkbox, then shift-click another: every row between them takes the same state — selected, or cleared if the shift-clicked row was selected. Ranges follow the rows as displayed (sorted and filtered). Turn it off with `enableBatchRowSelection: false`.

Example (`selection-actions`):

```tsx
function SelectionActionsExample() {
  const [data, setData] = React.useState(() => baseUsers.slice(0, 20))
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableRowSelection: true,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
    renderTopToolbarCustomActions: ({ table }) => (
      <table.Subscribe selector={(state) => state.rowSelection}>
        {(selection) => {
          const count = Object.keys(selection).length
          return (
            <Button
              size="sm"
              variant="destructive"
              disabled={count === 0}
              onClick={() => {
                setData((prev) => prev.filter((user) => !selection[user.id]))
                table.resetRowSelection()
              }}
            >
              <RiDeleteBinLine />
              Delete {count > 0 ? count : ""}
            </Button>
          )
        }}
      </table.Subscribe>
    ),
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

## Select-all behavior

The selection column header carries a select-all checkbox. `selectAllMode` controls its scope — `"page"` (default) toggles the current page, `"all"` toggles every row across pages. Set `enableSelectAll: false` to hide the header checkbox entirely.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableRowSelection: true,
  selectAllMode: "all", // "page" | "all"
  enableSelectAll: true,
})
```

## Relevant options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enableSelectAll` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the select-all checkbox in the selection column header. Default true. |
| `selectAllMode` | `"page" \| "all"` | `"page"` | Select-all scope for the header checkbox: the current page ("page", default) or every row ("all"). |
| `enableBatchRowSelection` | `boolean` | `true` | Shift-click a row's checkbox to select (or clear) every row since the last one clicked. Default true. |

## Related

- [useDataTable options](/docs/api/use-data-table)
- [Table instance](/docs/api/table-instance)
- [Export](/docs/guides/export)

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/row-ordering/ -->

# Row ordering

Set `enableRowOrdering: true` to add a drag-handle column for drag-and-drop row reordering.

You own the data: the table reports the move via `onRowOrderChange: (activeRowId, overRowId) => void`, and it is up to you to reorder your array. Provide `getRowId` so the ids passed to the callback are stable, and typically set `enablePagination: false` so dragging spans the full list.

Example (`row-ordering`):

```tsx
function RowOrderingExample() {
  const [data, setData] = React.useState(() => makeUsers(12))
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableRowOrdering: true,
    enablePagination: false,
    onRowOrderChange: (activeId, overId) =>
      setData((prev) => {
        const from = prev.findIndex((r) => r.id === activeId)
        const to = prev.findIndex((r) => r.id === overId)
        if (from === -1 || to === -1) return prev
        const next = [...prev]
        const [moved] = next.splice(from, 1)
        if (moved) next.splice(to, 0, moved)
        return next
      }),
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const [data, setData] = useState(initialData)

const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableRowOrdering: true,
  enablePagination: false,
  onRowOrderChange: (activeRowId, overRowId) => {
    setData((prev) => {
      const next = [...prev]
      const from = next.findIndex((row) => row.id === activeRowId)
      const to = next.findIndex((row) => row.id === overRowId)
      const [moved] = next.splice(from, 1)
      next.splice(to, 0, moved)
      return next
    })
  },
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

> **Not compatible with virtualization:** Row drag-and-drop is incompatible with row virtualization. Disable virtualization when you enable row ordering.

## Related

- [useDataTable options](/docs/api/use-data-table)
- [Table instance](/docs/api/table-instance)
- [Row selection](/docs/guides/row-selection)

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/row-dragging/ -->

# Row dragging

Rows can be dragged out of a table — onto another table, or onto a drop zone of your own — with the pointer, touch or the keyboard. (To reorder rows inside one table, see [Row ordering](/docs/guides/row-ordering).)

## Between tables

Wrap the tables in `DataTableDndProvider`, turn on `enableRowDragging` on the table rows leave from, and move the row in `onRowDragEnd`:

```tsx
import { DataTable, DataTableDndProvider, useDataTable } from "@/components/ui/data-table"

function Lists() {
  const [todo, setTodo] = React.useState(initialTodo)
  const [done, setDone] = React.useState(initialDone)

  const todoTable = useDataTable({
    data: todo,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableRowDragging: true,
    onRowDragEnd: ({ row, over }) => {
      if (over.type === "table" && over.table === doneTable) {
        setTodo((rows) => rows.filter((r) => r.id !== row.id))
        setDone((rows) => [...rows, row.original])
      }
    },
  })
  const doneTable = useDataTable({ data: done, columns, getRowId: (row) => row.id })

  return (
    <DataTableDndProvider>
      <DataTable table={todoTable} className="data-[drop-target]:ring-2 data-[drop-target]:ring-primary" />
      <DataTable table={doneTable} className="data-[drop-target]:ring-2 data-[drop-target]:ring-primary" />
    </DataTableDndProvider>
  )
}
```

`over` says where the row landed: `{ type: "table", table, rowId? }` (the table, and the row it was dropped on, if any) or `{ type: "zone", id }`. While a row from another table is over a table, the table's root has a `data-drop-target` attribute, so you can highlight it with `data-[drop-target]:…` classes. A floating preview follows the pointer.

Each table inside the provider keeps its own column and row reordering and drag-to-group, and the tables may share row and column ids.

## Drop zones

Make any element a drop target with `useDataTableDropZone(id)` inside the provider:

```tsx
import { useDataTableDropZone } from "@/components/ui/data-table"

function Trash() {
  const { setNodeRef, isOver } = useDataTableDropZone("trash")
  return (
    <div ref={setNodeRef} className={isOver ? "bg-destructive/10" : undefined}>
      Drop here to delete
    </div>
  )
}
```

A row dropped there calls `onRowDragEnd` with `over: { type: "zone", id: "trash" }`.

## Reordering too

`enableRowDragging` only adds the drag handle; combine it with `enableRowOrdering` (and `onRowOrderChange`) to reorder inside the table as well.

## Relevant options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enableRowDragging` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds a drag handle to each row for moving rows out of the table — to another table or a drop zone in the same `DataTableDndProvider` — without reordering inside it (combine with `enableRowOrdering` for both). Default false. |
| `onRowDragEnd` | `(props: { row: DataTableRow<TData> table: DataTableInstance<TData> over: RowDropTarget }) => void` |  | Called when a row is dropped on another table or a drop zone in the same `DataTableDndProvider`. Move the row in your data. |
| `enableRowOrdering` | `boolean` | `false` | Drag-and-drop row reordering (adds a drag-handle column). |
| `onRowOrderChange` | `(activeRowId: string, overRowId: string) => void` |  | Called on a row drag-and-drop reorder; the consumer reorders its data. |

## Related

- [Row ordering](/docs/guides/row-ordering)
- [Composition](/docs/guides/composition)

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/row-pinning/ -->

# Row pinning

Set `enableRowPinning: true` to add a pin toggle inside the row-number column. Pinned rows stick to the top while you scroll the rest of the table.

Because the toggle lives in the row-number column, row pinning pairs with `enableRowNumbers: true`.

Example (`row-pinning`):

```tsx
function RowPinningExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableRowNumbers: true,
    enableRowPinning: true,
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableRowNumbers: true,
  enableRowPinning: true,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

> **Enable row numbers:** Turn on `enableRowNumbers` so the pin toggle has a column to live in.

## Display modes

`rowPinningDisplayMode` sets where pinned rows show and how rows get pinned:

| Mode | Pinned rows | Pinned by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"top-and-bottom"` (default) | Stay in view above (or below) the other rows while scrolling | The pin button (to the top), or `row.pin("bottom")` |
| `"top"` / `"bottom"` | The same | The pin button, to that side |
| `"static"` | Listed first (or last), and scroll away with the rest | The pin button |
| `"select-top"` / `"select-bottom"` | Stay in view on that side | Selecting the row; deselecting unpins it. No pin buttons |

```tsx
useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  enableRowSelection: true,
  enableRowPinning: true,
  rowPinningDisplayMode: "select-top", // selected rows stay in view at the top
})
```

Sticky pinned rows need a bounded scroll surface, which the table has by default (see [Sticky header & footer](/docs/guides/sticky)).

## Related

- [useDataTable options](/docs/api/use-data-table)
- [Table instance](/docs/api/table-instance)
- [Row numbers](/docs/guides/row-numbers)

<!-- https://monabbir-ahmmad.github.io/shadcn-react-table/docs/guides/row-numbers/ -->

# Row numbers

Set `enableRowNumbers: true` to add a leading row-number column to the table.

Example (`row-numbers`):

```tsx
function RowNumbersExample() {
  const data = React.useMemo(() => baseUsers, [])
  const columns = useUserColumns()
  const table = useDataTable({
    data,
    columns,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    enableRowNumbers: true,
    rowNumberMode: "static",
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  })
  return <DataTable table={table} />
}
```

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableRowNumbers: true,
})

return <DataTable table={table} />
```

## Numbering mode

`rowNumberMode` controls how the numbers are computed:

- `"static"` (default) numbers the current view and is page-aware, so the first visible row on each page restarts the count appropriately.
- `"original"` uses the source row index, so each row keeps the same number regardless of sorting or pagination.

```tsx
const table = useDataTable({
  data,
  columns,
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  enableRowNumbers: true,
  rowNumberMode: "original",
})
```

> **Pairs with row pinning:** The row-number column is also where the pin toggle lives, so it works well alongside row pinning.

## Related

- [useDataTable options](/docs/api/use-data-table)
- [Table instance](/docs/api/table-instance)
- [Row pinning](/docs/guides/row-pinning)
